title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed law designed to protect the United States from risks associated with advanced artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes regulations that require developers to implement robust safety measures, conduct risk assessments, and promote transparency in AI development to safeguard national security and public welfare.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence use across key industries, aiming to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It outlines sector‑specific guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and enforcement provisions to promote responsible AI development and deployment while protecting public interests.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb the use of AI by businesses that inflate prices and manipulate wages. It proposes rules that would hold companies accountable for unfair AI-driven pricing and labor practices, aiming to protect consumers and workers alike.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House believes Congress should refuse to give extra funding or special regulatory help to AI firms or banks that are close to collapse because of AI market stresses. Instead, the focus should be on providing support to all Americans who have been harmed by these AI-related financial problems.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act introduces rules and safeguards for using AI in veterinary practice, focusing on animal welfare, data protection, and accountability. It sets clear standards for safety, transparency, and oversight to ensure AI tools benefit animal health while protecting the rights of all stakeholders.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that limits how artificial intelligence can be used in medical care, making sure that licensed doctors stay in charge of diagnosing and treating patients. It creates rules and oversight to prevent AI tools from replacing or overriding the expertise of human physicians.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is designed to make companies that use algorithms more transparent and fair. It would require them to evaluate their systems for bias and potential harm and report those findings to regulators and the public.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect electoral integrity by setting guidelines and regulations for AI usage in election contexts. It seeks to prevent AI-driven misinformation and manipulation, ensuring fair and trustworthy voting processes.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at ensuring that AI systems developed in the United States are safe, trustworthy, and reliable before they are released to the public. It establishes standards, testing procedures, and oversight mechanisms that researchers and developers must follow to minimize risks and promote responsible AI innovation.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires organizations in Virginia to publicly disclose how they use artificial‑intelligence systems, including the data and algorithms behind key decisions. The law also establishes standards for documenting AI impact, ensuring accountability, and protecting citizens from opaque or unfair AI practices.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules to make sure that any artificial‑intelligence tools used to process veterans’ claims are transparent, fair, and reliable. It requires clear documentation, regular audits, and oversight mechanisms so that the decisions made by AI can be reviewed, corrected, and held to high standards of accuracy and accountability.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This policy introduces an act designed to safeguard consumers against deceptive practices involving artificial intelligence. It outlines rules and enforcement measures to ensure transparency and accountability in AI deployments.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act proposes measures to strengthen the protection of AI systems against threats such as malicious manipulation and cyberattacks. It outlines requirements for developers and organizations to implement security protocols, conduct risk assessments, and cooperate with regulatory bodies to ensure the resilience and reliability of advanced artificial intelligence technologies.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a specialized team within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to address the security risks of artificial intelligence. The task force will evaluate AI technologies, develop best‑practice guidelines, collaborate with private companies, and help safeguard critical infrastructure from potential AI‑related threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a law that sets rules for how AI systems are developed, used, and monitored to reduce harmful outcomes. It requires companies and organizations to evaluate, document, and report potential AI risks, and it creates guidelines and enforcement mechanisms to keep AI safe for the public.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework for overseeing the deployment of AI in physical devices and machinery, ensuring safety, reliability, and compliance across industries. It creates standards, regulatory oversight, and coordination mechanisms among manufacturers, regulators, and users to manage risks associated with AI-driven physical systems.
